BERT4Rec’s random Cloze masking differs from terminal next-item inference. The original model includes last-item masking; earlier [recency-sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) explicitly identifies this mismatch. An inference-aligned hypothesis is to train on sampled prefixes ending in a reserved mask, withholding the target and subsequent interactions. Keep bidirectional attention over the visible prefix and read the appended mask’s representation. This is an experimental adaptation, not an established improvement for these four datasets.

Recent evidence supports testing multi-negative objectives while controlling sampling bias. [Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compare random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive negatives: results depend on dataset characteristics, and aggregate gains can conceal popularity-band disparities. [Correcting the LogQ Correction, RecSys 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) distinguishes the always-present positive from Monte Carlo-sampled negatives when deriving sampled-softmax correction. Sampling-probability correction addresses a different problem from false-negative correction; neither automatically solves the other.

For this benchmark, compare fixed-weight terminal-mask multi-negative softmax against the same objective with a modest fraction of model-mined hard negatives, holding backbone, training budget and auxiliary-loss weights constant. Exclude known training positives and duplicate candidates; treat remaining unobserved items as uncertain negatives. Older [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) motivates false-negative handling but uses a teacher mechanism, so its full recipe should not be imported into this single-model experiment. Select using the pinned macro validation HR@10: better sampled-pair margins alone do not establish better top-10 ranking.
